extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO disciplinary staff, and legal counsel involved in practitioner discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural outcomes for imposing reciprocal discipline on a USPTO-registered practitioner based on state-law suspension, including required notices, duties during suspension, and restrictions on USPTO accounts and PKI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a duly constituted authority of a State pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Notice and Order is sent to the respondent notifying them that a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline has been filed and providing an opportunity to file a response opposing identical discipline within forty (40) days. Failure to respond may lead to imposition of identical discipline after determination there is no genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's opportunity to oppose per 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may file a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the state based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order provides a 40-day period to file such a response. Successful opposition must identify and support one of the statutory bases in § 11.24(d)(1); absence of a timely response is treated as no genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to file a timely response
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response to the Notice and Order, the Office may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose the identical discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order here relies on Respondent's failure to file any response after being served (including emailed copy) to support suspension for ninety (90) days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation predicated on 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline can be predicated upon a respondent being suspended from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State, in violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order suspends the practitioner for violating § 11.804(h), where the underlying state suspension provided the predicate misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to impose discipline — statutory/regulatory basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary action before the USPTO is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final Orders will cite these authorities as the basis for imposing discipline and for publication and notification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is ordered to publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the suspension, practitioner identity, registration number, and the basis for discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample Notice includes practitioner's name and registration number, the length of suspension, the rule violated (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)), a summary of the underlying facts (e.g., failure to timely file a patent application and resulting prejudice), citation to the state disciplinary proceeding, and reference to the statutory/regulatory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to state disciplinary agencies and courts per 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures other jurisdictions and relevant courts are informed of USPTO disciplinary actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties during suspension per 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires compliance with § 11.58 but does not restate its contents; practitioners should consult § 11.58 for obligations such as client notification, file transfer, and other suspension-related duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate the respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative steps will be taken to remove the practitioner's ability to sign/submit filings tied to Customer Numbers and PKI until reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to USPTO Customer Numbers during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor have her name added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until she is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents suspended practitioners from circumventing suspension by using or obtaining access credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underlying professional-conduct failings (diligence, communication, disciplinary cooperation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The underlying state disciplinary agreement cited violations of Arizona Rules of Professional Conduct: 1.3 (diligence), 1.4 (communication), 8.1(b) (failure to respond in a disciplinary matter), and 54(d) (failure to cooperate and respond in a disciplinary matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The factual summary: respondent told a client she filed a non-provisional patent application in August 2011 but actually filed in August 2012; the late filing caused loss of priority when examiner cited a patent from a 2012 application; client later paid another attorney and the patent issued. These facts illustrate misconduct examples (lack of diligence and communication, misleading client, and failing to cooperate in disciplinary matters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the OED FOIA Reading Room (http://efoia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO publishes disciplinary outcomes for transparency and reference by practitioners and enforcement bodies.
